info.bio:
Wendy Carlos (nacida como Walter Carlos el 14 de noviembre de 1939 en Pawtucket (Rhode Island, EE.UU.) es una compositora de música electrónica estadounidense. Carlos fue una de las primeras intérpretes famosas de música electrónica que usaron sintetizadores.

Su primer disco Switched-On Bach (Conectado con Bach, -en Latinoamérica-Bach electrónico o —en España— Enchufado a Bach) fue tal vez el primer álbum en intentar el empleo de sintetizadores como una alternativa a la orquesta.

scenes.desc: La primera dosis de electrónica extrema para los chicos de Sheffield fue la banda sonora de Walter Carlos para La naranja mecánica; antes solo había atisbos en el Moog de Keith Emerson y los chorros de ruido de Eno en Roxy Music. Detrás asoman la música concreta, Morton Subotnick y los paisajes de Tangerine Dream.

scenes.name: Electrónica y rock
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: El sintetizador de Robert Moog (1966) revoluciona el rock hasta la última fibra. La vanguardia lo adopta primero (Morton Subotnick); después llegan Mort Garson, Ron Geesin, Walter Carlos (Switched On Bach, primer disco electrónico en las listas; Sonic Seasonings anticipa el ambient), Lothar & The Hand People, Silver Apples (dúo de teclados electrónicos que se adelanta una década a la new wave y el synth-pop), Beaver & Krause, David Borden, Bo Hansson y Tonto's Expanding Head Band. El Minimoog portátil (1970) lleva el sintetizador a los escenarios.

podcast.title: A Clockwork Orange Score (Early 1970s)
podcast.body: Walter Carlos composed the all-electronic score for Stanley Kubrick's movie *A Clockwork Orange*. The profits generated from these bold synthesizer experiments later funded a sex change operation. "after composing the all-electronic score for the Stanley Kubrick movie A Clockwork Orange."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Sex Change and New Identity
podcast.body: After achieving success with pioneering electronic music and film scores, Walter Carlos underwent a sex change operation, funded by the profits from these ventures. Wendy Carlos now lives and works in New York City. "The profits from those bold synthesizer experiments paid for a sex change operation, and now Wendy Carlos lives and works in New York City."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: A Clockwork Orange (1972) Score
xref.body: Wendy Carlos, a classical musician who had been collaborating with Bob Moog on the development and application of his new modular synthesizers, was hired by director Stanley Kubrick to compose the score for his 1971 futuristic dystopian film, *A Clockwork Orange*. The entirely electronic score, released as a soundtrack in 1972 (with Carlos identifying as Walter Carlos at the time), introduced sounds no one had heard before and became a landmark in the widespread development of electronic music, influencing many rock musicians seeking novel sounds. "No one had ever heard such sounds. It was completely electronic."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Identity Transition and Financial Independence
xref.body: Originally known as Walter Carlos, she later transitioned to Wendy. The money earned from her work on "A Clockwork Orange" soundtrack played a role in this personal journey. "She was Walter then, Wendy now. It took the money he made from the Clock of Orange soundtrack. Which is on a way, came back as Wendy."
